title: Unit – 4 : Session – 1 : SLO – 1  |  Trees — Introduction
sections: A TREE is a non-linear data structure used to represent hierarchical relationships.
The topmost node in a tree is called the ROOT.
A node that has no children is called a LEAF (terminal node).
A node having at least one child is called an INTERNAL (non-terminal) node.
A PARENT is a node that has one or more child nodes.
The nodes that are directly connected and come after a node are its CHILDREN.
The number of edges from the root to the node is called the DEPTH (level).
The length of the path from a node to the deepest leaf is called the HEIGHT.
A tree with no nodes is called an EMPTY (NULL) tree.
A tree in which each node has at most two children is called a BINARY tree.
The degree of a node is the number of its CHILDREN.
The ANCESTORS of a node includes all the nodes along the path from the node to the root.
A tree in which all leaf nodes are at the same level is a PERFECT BINARY TREE.
The tree data structure is used in many applications such as FILE SYSTEMS, DATABASE INDEXING and COMPILER DESIGN.
The total number of nodes in a full binary tree is 2^(h+1) - 1, where h is the height.
